title: JWT / bearer token
summary: alg=none, key confusion, unverified signatures, kid/jku tricks, role claims, expiry, and tokens in URLs.

groups.title: Signature and algorithm
groups.summary: If the signature is not verified, nothing else matters.

checks.title: alg=none
checks.why: The resource server accepts an unsecured JWT.
checks.validate: A token with alg=none and an empty signature is accepted as you.

variants.name: none with empty sig
variants.payload: Header: {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}\nPayload: copy a real token's claims, keep sub\nSignature: (empty)
variants.expect: Authorization: Bearer <header>.<payload>.   — trailing dot, empty sig. Must 401.
variants.why: Signing an arbitrary payload with alg=none and an empty signature bypasses verification.

variants.name: None / NONE / nOnE
variants.why: The alg check may be case-sensitive, so casing variants bypass an exact-string deny.

checks.title: HS256 with the RSA public key
checks.why: The server is configured for RS256 but will verify HS256 using the PEM public key as the HMAC secret.
checks.validate: A token you signed with HS256 and the published public key is accepted. Use a test account.

variants.name: RS256 → HS256
variants.payload: Take the realm's public key (JWKS or TLS). Sign a test-account token with HS256 using that PEM as the secret.
variants.expect: Must 401. A 200 on /me as that account is the finding.
variants.why: Switching from RS256 to HS256 lets you sign with the public key as the HMAC secret.

variants.name: alg allowlist
variants.payload: Try alg=HS256, HS384, HS512 against an RS256 API, and EdDSA / PS256 if you have keys.
variants.expect: Only the configured algorithms may verify.
variants.why: A server that checks only the claimed alg but not a fixed allowlist is the confusion vector.

checks.title: Signature not checked
checks.why: Any well-formed three-part token is trusted.
checks.validate: A token with a garbage signature is accepted.

variants.name: Flip the last byte
variants.payload: Take a valid access token, change the last signature character, send it.
variants.expect: Must 401. If /me still returns you, signatures are not checked.
variants.why: A corrupted signature that is still accepted means verification is skipped.

variants.name: Empty payload claims only
variants.payload: Craft a token with sub= of another test account and a random signature.
variants.expect: Must 401. Do not target a real user.
variants.why: Tokens carrying only benign claims are the cleanest test that no signature is required.

checks.title: kid / jku / x5u controlled keys
checks.why: kid is used as a path or SQL key, or jku/x5u fetches an attacker JWKS.
checks.validate: A token signed with a key you control is accepted, or kid triggers a callback / traversal.

variants.name: jku to your JWKS
variants.expect: An outbound fetch to your listener is a lead. Acceptance of a token signed by that key is the finding. Do not point jku at cloud metadata.
variants.why: Pointing jku at an attacker JWKS supplies the key the server uses to verify.

variants.name: kid path / SQLi
variants.expect: Must be an allowlisted key id. A file read, SQL error, or callback is the finding.
variants.why: kid is often used as a file path or SQL key, enabling path traversal or injection.

variants.name: embedded jwk
variants.expect: Embedded JWK must be ignored. A token signed by the matching private key must 401.
variants.why: A jwk embedded in the header can supply the verification key inline.

groups.title: Claims and transport
groups.summary: Roles, expiry, and where the token travels.

checks.title: Untrusted role / tenant claims
checks.why: The API trusts role, admin, or tenant_id inside a token the client can obtain or mint.
checks.validate: Raising a claim in a still-valid signature (or an accepted alg=none token) grants privilege.

variants.name: Raise role in a forged token
variants.payload: If alg=none or confusion worked, set role=admin / isAdmin=true / tenant_id of B and call an admin route.
variants.expect: Even if crypto held, try the same claims on a /me PATCH — mass assignment is the sibling finding.
variants.why: A forged role/tenant claim that is honoured is an authorization bypass.

variants.name: azp / aud / typ mix-up
variants.payload: Replay an id_token as an access token, or an access token issued for a sibling API.
variants.expect: aud and typ must be checked. A 200 on the wrong audience is the finding.
variants.why: Mismatched audience/type fields are parsed differently by client and server.

checks.title: exp / nbf enforced
checks.why: An expired access token or a reused refresh token still works.
checks.validate: A token past exp is accepted, or a rotated refresh token is replayed.

variants.name: Expired access token
variants.payload: Save an access token, wait for exp (or edit exp if signatures are not checked), replay /me.
variants.expect: Must 401. Clock skew of a minute is normal; hours are not.
variants.why: An accepted expired token means expiry is not enforced.

variants.name: Refresh replay
variants.payload: Refresh once, then replay the old refresh token.
variants.expect: The family must die. A second access token is the finding.
variants.why: Replaying a used refresh token means rotation is not enforced.

checks.title: JWT in the URL
checks.why: access_token= in a query, a hash fragment left in history, or a token in Referer.
checks.validate: A live token is observable in a URL, log, or Referer you are allowed to read.

variants.name: Token in query
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/me?access_token=<token> HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: If it works, the token is now in logs and Referer. Prefer that it does not work.
variants.why: A bearer in the query leaks into logs, caches, and Referer.

variants.name: Storage
variants.payload: DevTools → Application: localStorage / sessionStorage keys that hold a JWT.
variants.expect: A long-lived access token in localStorage is XSS→account takeover. Prefer memory or a cookie with the right flags.
variants.why: A token stored in accessible browser storage is readable by any script on the origin.

jwt-none.purpose: Signing an arbitrary payload with alg=none and an empty signature bypasses verification.
jwt-none.payload: Header: {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}\nPayload: copy a real token's claims, keep sub\nSignature: (empty)

jwt-role-claim.purpose: A forged role/tenant claim that is honoured is an authorization bypass.
jwt-role-claim.payload: If alg=none or confusion worked, set role=admin / isAdmin=true / tenant_id of B and call an admin route.
